record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.original_question: What experimental scan of strange-particle and strange-antibaryon yields and spectra across SPS, AGS, and RHIC energies, projectile-target sizes, and reaction volumes is needed to determine how collision energy and reaction volume combine to set the overall strangeness yield and to locate the deconfinement transition region?

evidence.quote: My personal experimental and theoretical priorities are as follows: Experiment
Complete analysis of SPS-158 A GeV, with the aim of presenting both particle spectra and precise relative hadronic/strange particle yields;
Determine the yield of strange antibaryons at the AGS Au-beam.
Obtain strange particle yields, and spectra, at the energy intermediate between AGS and maximum available at SPS, and compare with the lower/higher energy results in comparable conditions.

Ramp the energy of the SPS up to check if strangeness yield rises even with a (small) energy increase. Vary the size of projectile/target combination (e.g. using Ag–Ag collisions or/and trigger condition on heavy projectile/target combination) to see how energy and reaction volume combine to determine the overall strangeness yield.

In view of the likely phase-out of experimental research programs at AGS and SPS, and the likely occurrence of the deconfinement transition below the lower RHIC energy limit (4 times the current SPS-CM-available energy) commence development of a nuclear intersecting beam collider ranging the deconfinement transition region.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Design and carry out an experimental program in relativistic heavy-ion collisions that disentangles the dependence of strangeness production on collision energy from its dependence on reaction volume, and that pinpoints the energy/volume region in which a transition to a deconfined phase occurs. Concretely:

1. Measure transverse-momentum and rapidity spectra and 4π-integrated yields of strange hadrons (K±, K0S, Λ, Λ̄, Ξ−, Ξ̄+, Ω−, Ω̄+, φ) in nucleus–nucleus collisions at fixed-target AGS energies (≈ 10A GeV), at the full SPS energy (158A GeV) including a complete relative-yield analysis between non-strange and strange species, and at one or more SPS beam energies intermediate between AGS and 158A GeV.

2. In particular, determine the yields of strange antibaryons (Λ̄, Ξ̄+, Ω̄+) in Au+Au collisions at the AGS, where they had not been measured.

3. Extend the same set of strange and antistrange observables to RHIC collider energies (√sNN up to ≈ 200 GeV) so that data over the full AGS–SPS–RHIC range are available under comparable analysis conditions.

4. At each energy, vary the projectile–target system (light, intermediate, and heavy nuclei) and select event classes corresponding to different participant numbers, so as to scan the reaction volume independently of √sNN.

Using this two-dimensional scan in (√sNN, system size / reaction volume), determine quantitatively how collision energy and reaction volume combine to fix the total strangeness yield (e.g., the K/π and hyperon/π ratios and strangeness-suppression factor γs), and identify the region of (√sNN, volume) in which non-monotonic or threshold-like behavior signals the onset of deconfinement.
artifact.status_search_result: The proposed scan has been substantially carried through. NA49 completed the SPS energy scan (20–158A GeV) and reported the famous "horn" in K+/π+ near 30A GeV; NA61/SHINE has performed a two-dimensional scan in beam momentum (13A–158A GeV/c) and system size (p+p, Be+Be, Ar+Sc, Xe+La, Pb+Pb) including strange-hadron yields and spectra; RHIC BES-I and BES-II (STAR) extended strangeness measurements down to √sNN ≈ 3 GeV. AGS strange-antibaryon yields remain very sparsely measured. While the experimental program largely exists, a definitive localization of the deconfinement onset and a complete factorization of energy- vs. volume-dependence of strangeness production are still under analysis, so the underlying physics question is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: System size dependence of strangeness production in NA61/SHINE
status_evidence.snippet: NA61/SHINE performs a two-dimensional scan in beam momentum (13A–150/158A GeV/c) and system size (p+p, p+Pb, Be+Be, Ar+Sc, Xe+La, Pb+Pb).
status_evidence.claim: The proposed two-dimensional energy/system-size scan of strangeness has been implemented at the SPS.

status_evidence.title: Strangeness production in STAR beam energy scan
status_evidence.snippet: STAR has measured strange and multi-strange hadron production across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan.
status_evidence.claim: RHIC BES extends strangeness measurements over a wide √sNN range as called for.

status_evidence.title: RHIC BES-II
status_evidence.snippet: BES-II (2019–2021) explored the phase transition region with energies extending below nominal injection.
status_evidence.claim: Localization of deconfinement region is still under active experimental investigation.
